candidates: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:254 - Hung flusher process is never killed before respawn. The process is created with `mp_context.Process`, a `SpawnProcess`. That class derives from `BaseProcess`, not from `multiprocessing.Process`, so `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` is false. The old code called `self.process.kill()` unconditionally. Now a process flagged as "hang" is never killed, and a new process for the same shards is started next to it. Two flushers then work the same shards, and every hang leaks a process. The same wrong check in `join()` means `terminate()` never runs. Check against `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess` instead, or skip only `threading.Thread`.

tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_consumer.py:62 - Sleep in test is a no-op because time.sleep is monkeypatched. The test patches `time.sleep` to a no-op at the top, so `time.sleep(0.1)` here does nothing. The flusher is not actually given time to process after the drift change. `step.join()` sets `stopped` right away, so the flusher thread may stop before it flushes, which makes the test flaky. Wait with a real sleep or poll until `messages` is non-empty, for example with a saved reference to the original `time.sleep`.
